v1.feedback: Palette and form are excellent — sepia-on-parchment Molnár grid reads instantly. The boomerang concept maps cleanly to the linked idea, but the chaos amplitudes (0.15 position, 0.35 rotation) are subtle enough that the reversal sweep may not register as a dramatic swerve without close attention; consider doubling the peak-reversal amplitude so the top rows visibly shatter for a beat. The lateral camera sway (sin at 0.03 freq) is slow enough to pass but adds nothing a fixed camera wouldn't — consider removing it entirely for a stiller, more contemplative frame that lets the grid's own motion carry the piece.

v2.feedback: The return-wave restoration has a dead multiply (`settleT * 0.0`) so the 'boomerang return' never actually re-orders the grid — chaos just passes through and cells snap back to baseGradient without a visible settling animation. Fix this to `settleT * 0.6` or similar so the viewer sees order physically reassembling behind the returning wavefront. Additionally, consider giving the inner squares a slightly warmer stroke (e.g. #6b5e4f) to add a subtle duotone depth against the outer squares, reinforcing the Molnár layering without breaking the restrained palette.
